explain.say: Imagine a fleet of hundreds of ships carrying 27,000 people, sailing from China across the ocean to India and Africa, almost 90 years before Columbus. Look at the timeline: these are the voyages of Admiral Zheng He.

faq.a: Zheng He was a Chinese admiral of the Ming dynasty. Between 1405 and 1433 he led seven great voyages across the Indian Ocean to Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and East Africa.

faq.q: How big were Zheng He's ships?
faq.a: Old records say the biggest treasure ships were over 120 metres long, though many historians think 60 to 75 metres is more likely. Either way, they were far bigger than European ships of the time.
asks: How long were the treasure ships?

faq.a: Yes. His later voyages visited East African ports such as Mogadishu, Brava and Malindi.

faq.q: Why was a giraffe sent to China?
faq.a: Rulers exchanged gifts with the Ming emperor. A giraffe from East Africa came via Bengal in 1414, and many in China thought it looked like the qilin of legend, a lucky sign.

faq.q: Why did China stop the voyages?
faq.a: After 1433 new Ming leaders decided the voyages cost too much and turned their attention to defending the northern border.
asks: Why did the treasure fleets end?

facts: Zheng He led seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.
A giraffe brought to the Ming court in 1414 was celebrated as a qilin.

quiz.say: How many great voyages did Zheng He lead?
quiz.show: How many great voyages did Zheng He lead?
quiz.why: He led seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.

wrong.0: There were more than two; the fleet sailed seven times.
wrong.2: Twenty is too many; there were seven.

quiz.say: What surprising animal reached China in 1414?
quiz.show: What surprising animal reached China in 1414?
quiz.why: A giraffe from Africa arrived, and people thought it looked like the legendary qilin.

wrong.0: Elephants were already known in southern China.
wrong.2: Kangaroos live in Australia, which the fleet did not visit.
